evidence.section: 4.1 Temperature dependence on strain hardening rate
evidence.quote: The deformation twinning dynamically increases the capacity of dislocation accumulation and contributes to the steady-state /Theta1in stage II.
the atomic formation mechanisms of the HCP phase from the FCC phase is alternate SF generation

Deformation twinning, by constantly generating new boundaries and reducing the mean free path of dislocations during plastic deformation (“dynamic Hall–Petch”), produces a high degree of strain hardening and a significant increase in the UTS.
At cryogenic temperatures, the reduced CRSS of the HCP phase-transformation makes the transformation easier [57,58] and induces TRIP effects in Cr26Mn20Fe20Co20Ni14 HEA
